findings.reason: a worker following §37 would search for a read that does not exist, and either invent a fault to repair or stall on the mandatory reproduction, which is the same failure earlier reviews found in §35's first arm.
findings.text: §37's Why says "the stored wait was taken from a read of the queue that still listed the request being dropped", but nothing in the dispatch path can add a `run:` wait a request did not name: `derive_wait_refs` appends a request ref only from `node.after` (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:2467-2474`), `_queue_validated_waits` stores exactly those refs (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:266-292`), `queue_batch` builds `after` only from the entry's own `after` and never from the CLI flag (`reckon/crew/dispatch_batch.py:413`, `:564-570`; `reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:1099-1140`), and `_validated_batch_waits` reads `live` only to close cycle edges and attribute projects (`queue_admission.py:2531-2560`, `:2640-2665`) — it never adds a ref. The deliverable's own rule, "a request stores a `run:` wait only for a request its own dispatch named through `after`", is therefore already what the code does, so the prescribed repair targets a mechanism that is not there and the reproduction the node must first produce cannot be reached

findings.reason: a done-when whose first arm cannot fail and whose negative control cannot be built gives the node no red measurement, so the gate would certify a change that no test distinguishes from the status quo.
findings.text: the first case ("after the drop, a batch entry under the same section with no `after` stores only its plan's declared waits") passes on today's unfixed code, and its declared negative control, "restoring the read that adds the unnamed wait fails the first case", cannot be constructed because no such read exists; only the second case, which needs a pointer seeded with an unnamed `run:` wait (`_rederive_waits` keeps every stored `run:` ref in `own`, `queue_admission.py:3817-3820`), can fail on the current tree

findings.reason: without the declared wait the queue is free to run two implementable nodes onto one file at once, which is the collision the plan otherwise prevents by declaration.
findings.text: s37 declares no `plan-section-depends-on` entry although §31, still `implementable`, writes both of §37's write paths (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py` and `reckon/crew/dispatch_batch.py`), so the queue may launch both nodes onto the same modules in one pass; the plan applied exactly this serialisation to §35 and §36 (`s36: [s35]`), and an earlier review's finding on the same gap for §32 was acted on

findings.reason: the whole-plan drain could be dispatched before the dropped-request repair lands, so the dogfood measure would run on the behaviour §37 is meant to change.
findings.text: §14's `plan-section-depends-on` lists every implementable section through s36 but not `s37`, while §14's first sentence says the drain begins "once every other section has landed" and §37 rewrites `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py`, the module the drain's own admission pass runs on; the same omission was raised and acted on for s32, s33, s34, s35 and s36

response_events.note: §37's Why no longer claims a stale queue read adds the wait; it records that no dispatch path adds an unnamed run: wait, and targets _rederive_waits keeping every stored run: ref as the request's own, so an unnamed wait persists and a discard makes it fatal.
§37's cases now start from a pointer seeded with an unnamed run: wait, as observed, so each case and its control fail on today's code.
